name: Burg Bideneck Fließ
kurzbeschreibung: Bideneck Castle near Fließ at 1,050 m: proud spur castle from the 13th century in the Upper Court with a 30 m keep, swallowtail battlements, and noble history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fortified Bideneck Castle (historically also Burg Biedenegg) is perched on a steep rocky spur above Fließ in the Tyrolean district of Landeck at an altitude of around 1,050 meters. As a strategic key castle at the entrance to the Oberes Gericht (Upper Court) and located on the historic Roman road Via Claudia Augusta, this formidable hilltop castle forms one of the best-preserved and most impressive medieval fortress ensembles in the entire Tyrolean Oberland. With its 30-meter-high Romanesque keep and striking battlements, the fortress dominates the valley basin of the upper Inn.

Route & Requirements

The construction of the castle dates back to the early 13th century, first mentioned in documents in 1339 as a fief of the Counts of Tyrol. The castle was named after and built by the knightly Lords of Bideneck. Over the centuries, the fortress changed hands several times, including the Lords of Rottenburg and, from the 16th century, the esteemed Tyrolean noble family of Mohr. In the 16th century, the defensive structure was extensively expanded and adapted in the Renaissance style. A prominent architectural feature is the widely visible swallowtail battlement crown, which adorns the upper part of the palas and the keep, giving the fortress its distinctive, defensive appearance. The entire complex includes the deep curtain wall, the Zwinger (outer bailey) with loopholes, a baroque gatehouse, and the castle chapel of St. Joseph, re-consecrated in the 17th century. The castle remains in private ownership to this day and is lovingly maintained by the owner family.

Visit & Arrival

The exterior of Bideneck Castle, its defensive walls, and the access avenue can be viewed and photographed from the outside free of charge year-round. As the complex is inhabited and privately owned, the interiors are not regularly open to the public (exceptions: private tours by prior arrangement and selected cultural events). Arrival by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 or S16 to Landeck, then continue on the B180 (Reschenstraße) through the Landecker Tunnel to Fließ; from there, a narrow, paved mountain road leads up to the castle (limited parking spaces along the road at the castle entrance). By public transport: ÖBB to Landeck-Zams train station, then by Postbus line 210 to Fließ Dorf and continue on foot (approx. 20 minutes uphill).

Tips

From the castle forecourt and the surrounding meadows, there is a breathtaking panoramic view of the Inn River, the Inn Valley, and the glaciated peaks of the Ötztal Alps. Combine your visit to the castle with a trip to the renowned Archaeological Museum Fließ in the village center and the nearby prehistoric sacrificial site at Piller Sattel.
oeffnungszeiten: Exterior area freely accessible year-round; interiors private
